hyps.why: A conv sibling next to a pool adds learnable capacity the pool lacks.
A pooling sibling provides no learned features, so a conv on edge 5 adds more.
A 1x1 on edge 1 is a diverse sibling beside a 3x3 chain at node 2 and complements it.
An identical 3x3 sibling at node 2 is redundant and saturates.
A 1x1 sibling beside a 3x3 at the output node gives scale diversity.
A skip beside a strong conv shortcut adds an identity path that helps optimization through the chain.
A strong downstream 3x3 chain makes better use of a stronger first-stage conv.
A 1x1 behind a 1x1 adds little spatial capacity and saturates.
Pooling upstream blurs features, so a 3x3 conv downstream benefits less.
Extra skips on top of an existing direct skip add redundant identity paths with small gains.
